_comment: How much a transporter substrate's (releaser's) effect is blunted when a reuptake blocker occupies the same transporter. A fractional RANGE, never a point: the relation between transporter occupancy and subjective blunting is not 1:1, and a computed Hill occupancy against a sub-nanomolar Kᵢ saturates to ~100% and over-predicts. Keyed by transporter, because the band is a property of the competition rather than of either drug.

bands.notes: Pooled across controlled human studies of SSRI pretreatment before MDMA (citalopram, paroxetine, fluoxetine) by the Sarparast 2022 systematic review: subjective effects attenuated ~30–80%, physiological effects only ~6–14%, and body temperature not attenuated at all. Read as effect blockade, not danger — acute SSRI co-dosing lowers rather than raises serotonin-syndrome odds, and no reported case has MDMA as sole agent. That hyperthermia is the one effect SSRIs do NOT blunt is why the blunting must never be presented as a safety margin.
